title: The Beginnings of Pyrotechnology, Part II: Production and Use of Lime and Gypsum Plaster in the Pre-Pottery Neolithic Near East
version: Journal of Field Archaeology 15(2), pp. 219–244, DOI 10.1179/009346988791974501
lineage: Original microscopy and energy-dispersive X-ray analyses. Published article inspected at the Smithsonian repository. Sample 86-1 came from the Hebrew University collection and the article cites Perrot for its context.

passages.locator: p. 224, table 1, sample 86-1, and p. 226, Eynan discussion
passages.note: The authors identify the hard material of a bench-like feature as incompletely calcined lime plaster, with a small amount of aluminosilicate. The table supplies a sample identifier, but no excavation locus number.

The authors received 86-1 and 86-2 from the Institute of Archaeology collection at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, courtesy of Ofer Bar-Yosef. The footnote gives no supplying accession or field number for 86-1.
